recommendation: Run bun run typecheck separately first to catch type errors before slower test suite

fact: Long-running Bash tasks launched with run_in_background=true can deadlock and outlive the Claude session, accumulating CPU/disk/log damage for days
recommendation: Default to foreground with explicit Bash timeout parameter (300000–600000ms). Only use background when a verifiable termination condition exists, and always pair with BashOutput + KillShell before session end.

provenance.reference: om_event_bot 2026-05-08: 4 pytest zombies x 2 days, errors.log -> 926MB, false Telegram alerts under prod-bot identity

fact: Git reads ~/.config/git/ignore (XDG default) as a global gitignore automatically — core.excludesFile does NOT need to be set
recommendation: Before suggesting `git config --global core.excludesFile <path>`, check whether ~/.config/git/ignore already exists. If it does, git is already using it — just append to that file. Setting core.excludesFile to a different path silently overrides the XDG file. Verify with `git check-ignore -v <path>` to see which gitignore source actually matches.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 user asked to add settings.local.json to global gitignore — discovered it was already present via XDG default ~/.config/git/ignore with no core.excludesFile set

fact: Aura Companion silently downgrades bypassPermissions → acceptEdits when server runs as root
recommendation: web/server/cli-launcher.ts:495-518 auto-downgrades user-selected 'Agent' mode (bypassPermissions) to 'acceptEdits' when the Hono server runs under root (default for /root/aura-companion deployment) — claiming 'Claude Code rejects bypassPermissions when running with root/sudo'. UI shows 'Agent', runtime is acceptEdits — platform-level docstring drift. Override via env var COMPANION_FORCE_BYPASS_AS_ROOT=1 (untested whether Claude Code CLI actually accepts under root). Proper fix: run Aura Companion as non-root system user. Diagnostic: Composer badge shows 'acceptEdits' instead of 'bypassPermissions' for sessions launched with Agent mode.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 cli-launcher.ts source read + Composer badge observation

fact: pytest -k or pytest tests/ without PYTHONPATH=. fails collection on projects that use 'from src.xxx import' pattern
recommendation: auraengine uses bare 'from src.bot.xxx import' and 'from app.xxx import' imports in tests. Bare 'pytest tests/' fails with ModuleNotFoundError because src/ is not on sys.path. Always prefix with PYTHONPATH=.. Document this in conventions.md / README. Adds support for the broader anti-pattern feedback_no_ignore_failing_test_diagnose_first.md — the FIX is PYTHONPATH=., not --ignore=<failing-file>.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 Phase 1 + 1.5 verification — multiple sessions tripped the same gotcha

fact: SKILL.md description and references/ content can drift independently — description may claim one stack while references describe another
recommendation: Before extending or forking a skill pack with reference documents, READ AT LEAST ONE REFERENCE in full to verify the stack matches the SKILL.md description. Concrete case: council-review/SKILL.md described 'Python 3.10 + aiogram + SQLAlchemy + PostgreSQL', but references/quality-postgres.md was Next.js/Prisma/Neon. Forking under the wrong assumption would have re-targeted from a fictional baseline. Mitigation: at fork time, grep references/ for the stack keywords claimed by SKILL.md; if they don't appear, the description has drifted. Trust references over descriptions — references are where principles live.

provenance.reference: 2026-05-11 discovered drift between council-review/SKILL.md (claimed aiogram) and references/quality-postgres.md (actually Next.js/Prisma/Neon)

fact: Pickup-prompts authored mid-workstream can drift from later-committed PLAN/HANDOFF. Phase 3α surfaced this 3 times: sub-2B pickup said watson + abramov were '4 mirrors / 3-section / 220-270L' but PLAN said '2 mirrors aura-only / 2-section / 155-185L'; sub-2C pickup proposed dump #1 python_sage tokens for vanrossum but PLAN correctly used dump #3 vanrossum tokens; sub-2C pickup proposed different §-anchor naming. Runtime probe of on-disk panel-files + dispatcher SKILL.md greps resolved each case decisively; pickup was authorship drift.
recommendation: On pickup of a multi-session phase: read HANDOFF + PLAN + pickup-prompt; if they disagree on mirror count / section split / token source / line targets, probe runtime (`ls ~/.claude/skills/<panel>/agents/`, grep SKILL.md for citations, count panel files) BEFORE proceeding. Surface the disagreement at session start with runtime evidence; do NOT proceed silently with either side. Memory: feedback_multi_source_instruction_contradiction_defer_surface + feedback_handoff_narrative_vs_runtime_state (sister patterns).

provenance.reference: HANDOFF-phase-3-α-CLOSURE.md NR3 + D8 — 3 pickup-vs-PLAN drift incidents across sub-2B + sub-2C, all resolved by runtime probe

fact: Aura Companion's running CLI session cannot author code changes to its OWN source tree without racing the WS bridge it relies on. Symptom: HMR reload mid-edit drops the WS, the editing session loses streaming. Phase 3α + 3α' development worked around this by running ALL writer agents in separate tmux sessions on the same workspace; the in-CLI session acts only as orchestrator + consolidator + observer. Sibling of `feedback_process_ancestry_check_before_parent_restart` (don't restart your own parent).
recommendation: When the workspace == the running CLI's source tree: NEVER author code from the in-CLI Claude session. Spawn writer-tmux explicitly (`tmux new -d -s <name> 'claude --resume <session-id> ...'` OR fresh codex/claude), pass the pickup-prompt via /tmp/<task>-pickup.md, and use the in-CLI session ONLY for orchestration (status checks via gh / git / runtime probes) and documentation commits (markdown / jsonl, which don't trigger HMR conflict).

provenance.reference: User correction 2026-05-18 — Phase 3α arc done entirely in tmux to avoid self-modification race
